breakfast.name: Green Fig and Saltfish
instructions: Boil green bananas until tender
Sauté flaked saltfish with vegetables
Serve together
breakfast.description: Saint Lucia's national dish — boiled green banana with salt cod.

breakfast.name: Cocoa Tea
instructions: Grate cocoa stick, boil in water with spices
Add milk and sugar
Strain, serve hot
breakfast.description: Rich hot cocoa from local cocoa sticks.

breakfast.name: Bakes with Saltfish
instructions: Bakes are St. Lucian fried dough -- similar to but distinct from Johnny cakes
The dough is softer and slightly sweeter than Johnny cakes
Fried until golden -- the outside is crispy, inside is soft
Split and filled with the saltfish sauté
Saltfish sauté: soaked, shredded salt cod with tomato, onion, and peppers
breakfast.description: Saint Lucian fried dough bakes split and filled with saltfish sauté (shredded salt cod with tomato, onion, and peppers). The bake is slightly sweeter and softer than a Johnny cake; the filling is savory. The St. Lucian breakfast combination.

breakfast.name: Green Fig and Saltfish
ingredients: Green figs (unripe bananas -- the St. Lucian term)
instructions: In St. Lucia, fig means banana -- green figs are unripe bananas
The confusion: St. Lucians say fig where others say banana
Green figs and saltfish is the St. Lucian national dish
The unripe bananas are boiled until tender -- they become starchy and potato-like
The saltfish sauté is the savory counterpart
Green figs and saltfish: the national dish, eaten at any meal
breakfast.description: Saint Lucia national dish -- boiled unripe bananas (called green figs in St. Lucian Creole) with saltfish sauté (rehydrated salt cod with tomato, onion, and Scotch bonnet). The unripe banana is starchy and potato-like when cooked. Eaten at breakfast, lunch, or dinner.

lunch.name: Bouyon (Thick Stew)
instructions: Boil salt meat until tender
Add root vegetables and coconut milk
Add dumplings
Cook until everything is tender
lunch.description: Thick one-pot stew with root vegetables.

lunch.name: Lambi (Conch) Creole
instructions: Tenderize and dice conch
Sauté vegetables and herbs
Add conch, simmer 20 min
Serve with rice

lunch.name: Callaloo Soup
instructions: Callaloo soup is the Caribbean leafy green soup -- one of the oldest dishes
Callaloo: the leaves of the dasheen (taro) plant or the amaranth plant
The leaves are cooked down in coconut milk until soft and the soup thickens
Crab or salt pork are the traditional protein additions
The okra adds additional thickening
Callaloo soup is a Caribbean-wide dish -- each island has its own version
lunch.description: Caribbean callaloo soup -- dasheen (taro) leaves cooked down in coconut milk with crab or salt pork, onion, garlic, and Scotch bonnet until the leaves are soft and the soup is thick and green. Okra optional for extra thickening. Each Caribbean island has its version.

lunch.name: Pumpkin Soup
ingredients: Pumpkin (Caribbean pumpkin -- denser and more flavorful than Halloween pumpkin)
instructions: Caribbean pumpkin is different from Halloween pumpkin -- denser, more flavorful, less watery
The Caribbean pumpkin: calabaza or similar varieties, orange-yellow flesh
Roasted or boiled pumpkin with aromatics
Blended smooth with coconut milk for richness
The Scotch bonnet gives heat but the coconut milk softens it
lunch.description: Saint Lucian pumpkin soup -- Caribbean pumpkin (denser and more flavorful than Halloween varieties) blended smooth with coconut milk, onion, garlic, and a Scotch bonnet for heat. The coconut milk softens the heat.

lunch.name: Bouyon (One-Pot Creole Stew)
ingredients: Root vegetables: dasheen, yam, cassava, sweet potato
instructions: Bouyon is the St. Lucian one-pot Creole stew -- a complete meal in a pot
Everything goes into one pot: meat, ground provisions (root vegetables), and dumplings
The ground provisions: dasheen, yam, cassava, sweet potato -- the Caribbean root vegetables
The term ground provisions: vegetables grown underground -- the traditional term
Callaloo leaves and okra added toward the end
Bouyon takes hours -- the long cooking melds everything together
lunch.description: Saint Lucian one-pot Creole stew -- pork or crab with ground provisions (dasheen, yam, cassava, sweet potato), plantain, callaloo leaves, okra, and dumplings, all cooked together until everything melds. Takes 1.5-2 hours. The term ground provisions means root vegetables grown underground.

dinner.name: Grilled Fish with Creole Sauce
ingredients: Creole sauce: tomato, onion, pepper, garlic, thyme, scotch bonnet
instructions: Season fish with lime and salt
Grill until flaky
Make creole sauce
Spoon sauce over fish
dinner.description: Grilled fish in spicy Creole sauce.

imageCredit.author: Photo by Victor Monsour of Monsour's Photography

dinner.name: Callaloo Soup
instructions: Boil callaloo until tender
Add coconut milk, okra, crab
Season and simmer until thick
dinner.description: Thick green soup with coconut and crab.

dinner.name: Grilled Mahi-Mahi with Creole Sauce
ingredients: Creole sauce: tomatoes, onion, peppers, thyme, garlic
instructions: Mahi-mahi (dorado) is caught in St. Lucian waters
Marinated with lime, garlic, and thyme
Grilled until just cooked through
Creole sauce: the St. Lucian tomato-based sauce with aromatics
The Creole sauce poured over the grilled fish
dinner.description: Saint Lucian grilled mahi-mahi with Creole sauce -- mahi-mahi marinated in lime and garlic, grilled, served with Creole tomato sauce (tomatoes, onion, peppers, Scotch bonnet, thyme). Fresh catch from St. Lucian waters.

dinner.name: Accra (Saltfish Fritters)
instructions: Accra are the Caribbean saltfish fritters -- from the West African acarajee
The name accra traces to the Yoruba acarajee (bean fritters) -- West African heritage
Salt cod is the Caribbean adaptation -- fish instead of beans
The flaked salt cod is folded into a seasoned flour batter
Fried until golden and crispy outside
Served with lime and hot sauce
dinner.description: Saint Lucian saltfish fritters (accra) -- flaked rehydrated salt cod folded into seasoned flour batter and fried until golden. The name traces to the Yoruba acarajee (West African bean fritters): salt cod is the Caribbean adaptation. Served with lime and hot sauce.

dinner.name: Stewed Oxtail
instructions: Stewed oxtail is the Caribbean slow-cook celebration dish
Oxtail: the tail of the cow -- a tough, collagen-rich cut that needs hours
The collagen breaks down into gelatin after 2-3 hours of braising
The result: a thick, luxurious sauce that coats the meat
Butter beans added near the end -- they absorb the sauce
Browning sauce (caramelized sugar) gives the dark color
dinner.description: Caribbean stewed oxtail -- oxtail braised for 2-3 hours with browning sauce, garlic, thyme, and Scotch bonnet until the collagen breaks down into a thick, gelatin-rich sauce. Butter beans added near the end. Celebration food: the long cooking time marks it as special.

snacks.name: Accras (Salt Cod Fritters)
instructions: Soak and flake cod
Mix with batter
Fry spoonfuls until golden

snacks.name: Roast Corn
instructions: Roasted corn is the St. Lucian roadside snack
Corn roasted directly over charcoal
The kernels char slightly -- the char gives sweetness and smoke
Brushed with butter and salted
Sold by street vendors throughout St. Lucia
The best corn is the local yellow variety -- sweet and fresh
snacks.description: Saint Lucian roadside roasted corn -- corn on the cob grilled directly over charcoal until the kernels char slightly, brushed with butter and salted. Sold by street vendors throughout the island. The slight char gives sweetness and smoke.

snacks.name: Coconut Sugar Cake
instructions: Coconut sugar cake is made by cooking grated coconut with brown sugar
The sugar caramelizes and coats the coconut
Dropped onto wax paper in mounds to set
The candy hardens as it cools
Ginger gives a warm spice note
Sold at markets and school tuck shops throughout the Caribbean
snacks.description: Caribbean coconut candy -- grated fresh coconut cooked with brown sugar and ginger until the sugar caramelizes and coats the coconut, dropped in mounds to set firm. Sold at markets and school tuck shops.

snacks.name: Pastelle
ingredients: Minced meat filling (beef or pork with olives, capers, raisins)
instructions: Pastelle is the St. Lucian Christmas food -- a steamed cornmeal parcel
A legacy of Spanish Caribbean influence
The cornmeal dough is softened with butter
Filled with a savory-sweet mince (the sweet elements: raisins and capers)
Wrapped in banana leaf and steamed
Made only at Christmas: the pastelle-making is a family event
snacks.description: Saint Lucian Christmas cornmeal parcel -- seasoned cornmeal dough filled with savory-sweet minced meat (olives, capers, raisins), wrapped in banana leaf and steamed. Made exclusively at Christmas; the pastelle-making is a family event. Spanish Caribbean heritage.

desserts.name: Banana Bread
instructions: Mash bananas
Mix with other ingredients
Bake at 175°C 60 min
desserts.description: Moist banana bread with island nutmeg.

desserts.name: Breadfruit Pudding
instructions: Ripe breadfruit has a creamy, sweet interior -- different from unripe breadfruit
Mashed and combined with coconut milk, sugar, and spices
Baked until set like a bread pudding
The coconut milk and spices carry the Caribbean flavor
desserts.description: Saint Lucian ripe breadfruit pudding -- ripe breadfruit (sweet and creamy when ripe) mashed with coconut milk, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, and eggs, baked until set. The Caribbean flavors: coconut, warm spice, tropical sweetness.

desserts.name: Banana Cake
instructions: Caribbean banana cake uses overripe bananas
The black bananas are the best: maximum sweetness
The rum is optional but traditional -- a St. Lucian touch
Spiced with cinnamon and nutmeg
desserts.description: Saint Lucian banana cake -- overripe (blackened) bananas mashed into a spiced cake batter with cinnamon, nutmeg, and an optional splash of rum. The blacker the banana, the sweeter the cake.

drinks.name: Rum Punch
instructions: Mix rum, lime, syrup, bitters
Serve over ice
Grate nutmeg on top

drinks.name: Seamoss Drink
instructions: Soak sea moss overnight
Boil until dissolved
Blend with milk and spices
Chill

drinks.name: Rum Punch
ingredients: Rum (local Saint Lucian rum -- Chairman's Reserve)
instructions: Rum punch is the Caribbean welcome drink -- served at every gathering
The Caribbean rum punch formula: one of sour (lime), two of sweet (syrup), three of strong (rum), four of weak (juice)
Saint Lucia produces its own rum: Chairman's Reserve from the Windward Islands Rum Distillery
The Angostura bitters: a dash on top -- the aromatic finish
Served over ice with a slice of lime
drinks.description: Saint Lucian rum punch -- the Caribbean formula: one part lime juice (sour), two parts sugar syrup (sweet), three parts rum (strong), four parts juice (weak), with a dash of Angostura bitters. Chairman's Reserve is the local Saint Lucian rum. Served over ice at every gathering.
